problem: Existing universal zero-shot goal navigation methods rely either on broad semantic exploration or on fine-grained graph-based target verification, and become inefficient when semantic cues are sparse, ambiguous, or insufficient for reliable graph matching.
motivation: A single agent should find object categories, specific instances, and text-described goals in unseen environments without task-specific training. Which strategy works best depends on the situation, so a planner should adapt between coarse search and fine target confirmation.
key_idea: A training-free planner that adaptively switches among geometric exploration, semantic exploration, partial-match exploration and target verification, guided by semantic-score dispersion and graph-matching confidence, and orders frontiers with a TSP solver.
insight: The abstract says that ablations support adaptive switching, context-aware semantic mapping and TSP-based frontier ordering as contributing components. It also reports a foundation-model analysis. Only the abstract was available, so specific ablation figures are not known.
method: Context-aware semantic value mapping: builds a semantic value map of the scene that takes context into account to score how promising each region is for the goal
Graph-based target verification: matches a scene graph against a goal graph to confirm candidate targets, with a matching confidence
Adaptive mode switching: chooses among geometric exploration, semantic exploration, partial-match exploration and target verification using semantic-score dispersion and graph-matching confidence
TSP-based frontier ordering: orders frontiers by solving a travelling-salesman-style problem to shorten exploration paths

results: ForesightNav beats UniGoal on ObjectNav across the three benchmarks (MP3D, HM3D, RoboTHOR), with the largest gain on RoboTHOR (+18.6 SR, +11.4 SPL). On HM3D it reaches 65.3% SR on InstanceNav and 29.6% SR on TextNav.
